page: Microsoft Azure D16als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dalsv7 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It has no local storage or bundled GPUs, but is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also achieve top-tier throughput. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks demonstrate average performance, while LLM inference speeds for text generation using a small 135M model reach top-tier levels.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio and high clock-speed AMD processor, the D16als_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, making it unsuitable for large-scale deep learning training or storage-intensive database clusters. It is best suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, image processing, lightweight LLM inference, and general compute-bound workloads.
